title: EDGE-A190 2v2 Breakout Support Game
source_text: 2v2 with multiple support players - players behind net try to break puck out. Players on sides are support and must pass. Source constraints shown: support below the goal line / behind the net and support above the circles.
game_problem: Break the puck out of pressure by recognizing and using available support options.
representative_information: 2v2 pressure, support-player locations, passing lanes, boards, goal line and circle boundaries.
player_decisions: Players in the 2v2 choose when and which support option to use to escape pressure and advance possession.
space_organization: End-zone 2v2 with multiple constrained support players positioned behind the net/below the goal line and above the circles.
coach_notes: Keep support players available but constrained to their source areas so the puck carrier must read pressure and choose the useful outlet.
adaptation_text: Use short possession bouts and restart quickly on a clean breakout, turnover, or out-of-bounds puck. Rotate support and interior roles frequently.
source_boundary: 2v2 breakout game, support-player locations and passing constraint are source-derived. Work interval, restart and rotation guidance are Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A544 Retrieval Under Forecheck Pressure
source_text: One player retrieves puck under pressure. Coach holds stick in the air or on the ice. If stick is on the ice, player passes to coach, who bumps it back. If stick is in the air, player skates puck around pile for a shot. Forechecker chases the entire rep and can steal puck and go in for shot. Both players stay in front for deflection and rebound from next rep. Alternate sides.
game_problem: Retrieve under forecheck pressure, read a coach cue, and choose pass support or carry-to-shot while protecting the puck.
representative_information: Forechecker pressure, coach stick cue, puck location, available pass/carry option, net and rebound traffic.
player_decisions: Retriever reads the coach cue and pressure, then passes or carries; forechecker angles and can convert a turnover into a scoring chance.
space_organization: Half-ice retrieval/forecheck station run from alternating sides with net-front continuation after the initial play.
coach_notes: The coach stick is an information cue, not a scripted route. Keep the forechecker live through the entire rep.
adaptation_text: Use age-appropriate legal pressure/contact. Keep the next puck ready so the previous pair's net-front deflection/rebound role flows directly into the next rep.
source_boundary: All core rules, cue logic, live forechecker, net-front continuation and alternating sides are source-derived. Safety wording and flow emphasis are Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A1241 Goalie Rebound Control Game
source_text: Players position as shown (both ends of ice can be used). Drill begins with Coach shot on goalie pads (to avoid stoppage of play). Players attempt to score by taking shots WITHOUT moving from their positions. Goalie attempts to control rebound. Drill stops with goal or when Goalie covers puck. Alternate goalies and players after 3-4 runs.
game_problem: Goalie controls rebounds while nearby shooters react to loose pucks without changing their starting positions.
representative_information: Initial pad shot, rebound direction, shooter locations, puck availability and cover/goal outcome.
player_decisions: Goalie chooses rebound-control response; shooters read the rebound and decide whether/when they can finish from their fixed positions.
space_organization: Goalie station at the net with four shooters positioned around the crease/slot area; can be run at both ends.
coach_notes: Use a controlled initial pad shot as written. Emphasize rebound placement/control and tracking the second puck action.
adaptation_text: Keep repetitions short and rotate goalies/players after the source's 3-4 runs. Adjust shooter distance only if needed to keep the challenge age-appropriate.
source_boundary: Setup, initial pad shot, fixed shooter positions, goalie rebound-control goal, stopping conditions and 3-4-run rotation are source-derived. Challenge-adjustment note is Carolina EDGE adaptation.

title: EDGE-A1364 3v3 Neutral-Zone Regroup Transition Game
source_text: 3v3 NZ Regroup Game - one team designated as O to start. When team carries the puck out of their zone, they must regroup with D inside blue line and head back into zone. Every time the defensive team takes the puck out, there is a regroup and transition through NZ.
game_problem: Transition from defense to offense through a neutral-zone regroup while maintaining 3v3 pressure and support.
representative_information: Possession change, blue-line exit, defenseman support inside the blue line, opponent pressure and re-entry space.
player_decisions: Possession team identifies the regroup option and reorganizes support for re-entry; defenders transition roles immediately when possession changes.
space_organization: 3v3 game using an attacking zone plus neutral-zone regroup space with a support defenseman inside the blue line.
goalie: ONE GOALIE PER SOURCE TITLE / DIAGRAM
coach_notes: The regroup requirement is the constraint; do not prescribe the pass sequence or re-entry lane.
adaptation_text: Keep play continuous through possession changes. If the regroup becomes automatic rather than read-based, vary defender pressure or support positioning rather than adding a scripted route.
source_boundary: 3v3 game, designated starting offense, mandatory regroup after zone exit and repeated NZ transition are source-derived. Pressure/support adjustment guidance is Carolina EDGE adaptation.
